_doc: Binds the UX scenarios S1-S11 in specs/perf-latency-program.md to the KPI names recorded in kpi-ledger.json, and to the budget each must meet. Read by scripts/perf/kpi_scorecard.py (`just perf-kpis`). The scenario set here must match the spec exactly; the scorecard fails loudly when they drift, because a scorecard that silently drops a scenario reports a clean board by having no checks. A scenario with an empty `kpis` list is NOT a pass: it is a scenario nobody can score, which is the state the scorecard exists to make visible.
direction_note: `lower_is_better` false means a bigger number is better (frames per second, throughput). `budget` is the spec's Target, `acceptable` its Acceptable, `breaking` its Breaking. Units follow the ledger entry's own unit.

S1.title: Audible integrity while playing (no dropout, xrun or glitch)
S1.missing_kpi: xruns_per_playing_hour, and silent_while_playing_events_per_hour now that PR #856 detects both a silent output and a stalled presentation clock. The sentinel proves the INSTRUMENT is quiet at idle; it does not yet report the RATE during a real set, which is the number S1 is about.

S2.title: Play or cue press-to-audible, autosync off
S2.missing_kpi: Both KPIs are being instrumented now (branch af--press-to-audible). Until a real capture lands, this scenario is UNMEASURED, and the transport_scheduled_offset_ms figure must NOT be read as a proxy: it starts counting after the press has already been handled, so it cannot see the input queueing that the user feels.

S3.title: Play pressed with autosync on (quantized launch)
S3.missing_kpi: Feature not built. Needs S2's instrumentation first to prove its phase-lock budget, so this stays unscored by design, not by neglect.

S4.title: Waveform smoothness while playing
S4.missing_kpi: p95 rAF frame delta and dropped-frame percentage per 10s window. PR #1126 added a visual-stutter KPI and PR #1176 cut per-frame rescans, but neither reports a p95 frame delta, and the audio-health Hz meter measures engine presentation ticks, not canvas paint, so a stuttering canvas still reads green.

S5.title: Deck load to playable (mix path)
S5.missing_kpi: The ledger holds a WORST case and a throughput, not a p95 over a named window. The boot-window and settled figures are the same scenario measured under two conditions and should be scored separately, because a user meeting the app for the first time only ever experiences the boot-window one.

S6.title: Deck load to stems-ready, deck already playable
S6.missing_kpi: The measured 14.8s figure is a load where stems sit ON the critical path, so it scores the CURRENT design, not this scenario. This scenario only becomes scoreable once mix-first loading lands and playability is separable from stems-ready.

S7.title: Library filter keystroke to render
S7.missing_kpi: p95 over a real typing session. The recorded 80ms is a settle time from a controlled run, not a keystroke distribution, and the spec's budget is explicitly a p95.

S8.title: Whole-collection search round trip
S8.missing_kpi: No timing at all; only a boolean searching flag exists. The lyric-search work landed a typed result-latency boundary (PR #1397) but wires no KPI yet.

S9.title: All Tracks pane time to interactive
S9.missing_kpi: The walk time is a SERVER-side cost per poll, not the pane's time to interactive, which is what a user waits on. Scoring one against the other would flatter the app.

S10.title: Row-select prefetch ready before a plausible load click
S10.missing_kpi: Only a hit or miss flag is recorded, with no duration, so the prefetch can be losing its race every time and still report hits.

S11.title: App cold start to first browse
S11.missing_kpi: Nothing measures launch to usable. This is the composite a first-time user actually meets, and the 8038ms boot-window fetch wall says it is likely the worst number in the app.

proxy_note: `proxy_only` marks a scenario whose only bound KPI measures something ADJACENT to what the scenario is about (a server-side cost standing in for a user-visible wait, a settle time standing in for a p95, an idle instrument check standing in for a rate during a real set). Such a scenario reports UNMEASURED with its reason, never PASS. It is set by hand, deliberately, because the flattering direction is the automatic one: on Wed 9 Sep 2026 the first run of the scorecard scored three of these PASS off their own notes saying they did not measure the scenario.
